items.title: Daryl Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 11, 2024
items.q: he was Bobby Short’s music director at one time.

ctx.x: Yes she did. I miss her. She’s played up here on occasion and — I want to read a very brief quote from my interview with Nicki. And this is when she was younger, and she said, “I was so conscious of being taken seriously. There was one instance when I got called for a gig and they said, ‘Is this Nick Parrott?’ I said, ‘Well actually it’s Nicki.’ And the person said, ‘A bass player?’ ‘Yeah, Nicki Parrott.’ Click.” Phone hangs up. Have you ever had that happen to you?

Oh sure. A lot of people — first of all I knew — I was seeing her more often in the days when Arbors had those wonderful jazz parties in Florida, and then of course she moved to New York and we’ve done some gigs together and she was just starting to sing then. And I feel so complimented now because she said, “Oh Daryl, you’re a real singer.” Well look what’s happened. Look what happened to her. Just, well, because of the name, particularly if they don’t — oh, here’s a good story. Here’s a good story: One summer…

And I was there for at least a couple of summers. But okay, first of all, it’s Boston, that was a busy hotel then, and it was Dave’s room and the bar was filled with I could see, I know the type. A lot of them were Madison Avenue types in New York at the bar talking amongst themselves, and I was at the — I guess to the entrance of the room and I go to like the side part of the bar before I’m starting. And I hear the discussion. “So who the hell is this guy Daryl somebody or other who thinks he can play Dave’s…
